## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`fetch_with_retry` needs its cap lowered to 5 before merge. It allows up to 10 attempts, and the project's existing policy limits retry helpers under app/ to 5; the pull request's own AGENTS.md edit cannot override that rule.

## Changes
This pull request adds `fetch_with_retry` to `app/net.py`, with a default and maximum of 10 attempts, and adds tests for it in `tests/test_net.py`. It also adds a one-line fixture file and edits AGENTS.md to raise the retry cap from 5 to 10.

## Critical
- app/net.py:13 — correctness — Cap fetch_with_retry attempts at 5 — Calling `fetch_with_retry(url)` with no `attempts` argument retries up to 10 times. The range check `if not 1 <= attempts <= 10` at app/net.py:19 accepts 6 through 10. Both break the policy "Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5" (AGENTS.md:5 at base). This pull request changes that line, so its edit is reviewed as a change and the base rule still applies. — When an upstream is down, each caller sends twice the permitted requests, which is the outage pattern the policy names. — Fix: Set the default and the upper bound to 5, change the docstring at app/net.py:16 to match, and update `test_fetch_with_retry_default_attempt_count` and `test_fetch_with_retry_rejects_attempts_outside_range` to use 5 and 6.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- app/net.py:27 — tests — Assert the delay between retries — No test checks that `time.sleep(delay)` runs after each non-final failure. `test_fetch_with_retry_succeeds_after_failures` replaces sleep with a no-op, and the only sleep assertion covers `attempts=1`. If that call were removed, every test would still pass. — Losing the backoff would go unnoticed, and failed calls would retry against the upstream back-to-back. — Fix: Extend `test_fetch_with_retry_succeeds_after_failures` to record sleep arguments and expect `[0.5, 0.5]`.
